evidence.excerpt: Solder joint degradation under repeated thermal excursions alters joint resistance in ways that can shift in-circuit test measurements outside tolerance windows, producing false failures or masking real defects. This study subjected 120 FR-4 boards, each carrying 84 SOIC-16 and 48 QFN-32 packages, to 0–100 °C thermal cycling at 2 cycles per hour for 500, 1000, and 1500 cycles. Joint resistance was measured with a four-wire Kelvin technique after each milestone. In-circuit test pass rates were re-evaluated at each stage using a bed-of-nails fixture on a commercial ICT platform. Results show that mean joint resistance increased by 38 mΩ after 1500 cycles for QFN pads, causing a 6.1 % increase in false-open calls. A temperature-corrected threshold model is presented that reduces false calls to below 1 % across all cycle counts tested. The model parameters are extracted from a 15-minute characterisation run on a fresh board.
